mainTopic: How a vessel joins (צירוף כלי) separated parts of a מנחה, for טומאה and for קמיצה
overview: This amud deals with the rule that a כלי joins (מצרף) everything inside it for קדשים. An עשרון of flour was split into two halves and placed in one bowl without the halves touching. רב כהנא rules that a טבול יום who touches one half disqualifies both, because the משנה says the vessel is 'מצרף', not 'מחבר'. He adds two limits: a vessel only joins what needs the vessel, and only a כלי חרס passes on טומאה through its airspace. רב כהנא then asks whether this joining is strong enough, from the Torah, to let a קומץ taken from one half count for the other. Two proofs are brought, one from a משנה about mixed מנחות and one from a ברייתא on 'וְהֵרִים מִמֶּנּוּ'. Both are pushed off, because each could be about parts that still touch somewhere, so the question stays unresolved. רבי ירמיה asks whether a vessel's joining and a water connection can work together, and his question ends in תיקו. Finally, רבא asks whether an already-impure half is 'full' of טומאה (שבע לו טומאה). אביי starts to challenge that idea from a משנה about an impure sheet, and his proof continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Two separate parts in one bowl: does touching one disqualify both?
steps.stepSummary: An עשרון was split into two halves and placed in one bowl, and a טבול יום touched one half. Does the rule that a vessel joins its contents apply even when the parts do not touch each other?
steps.simpleTranslation: [The עשרון was split into two halves] and put into a bowl, and a טבול יום touched one of the halves. What is the law? When we learned that a vessel joins what is inside it for sacred food, does that apply only where the contents touch each other, but not where they do not touch? Or perhaps there is no difference?
steps.whatsHappening: בני רבי חייא ask רב כהנא whether a bowl joins two separated portions of flour, so that touching one disqualifies the other too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה teaches that a כלי is מצרף its contents for קדשים, so טומאה in one part spreads to all. The question is whether that only works when the contents physically touch, or even when they lie apart in the same vessel.

keyTerms.meaning: A bowl or receptacle
Someone who immersed today and must wait for nightfall to be fully pure; he disqualifies קדשים he touches
A vessel joins its contents, so they count as one unit for טומאה
Sacred food, such as offerings
Or perhaps; it introduces the second side of a question

phrases.english: and placed it in a bowl,
and a טבול יום touched one of them,
what is the law?
When we learned: a vessel joins
what is inside it, for sacred food,
does that apply only where they touch each other,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הֵיכָא דְּלָא נָגְעִי בַּהֲדָדֵי – לָא,
phrases.english: but where they do not touch each other, not,
or perhaps there is no difference?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ? כִּי תְּנַן: כְּלִי מְצָרֵף מַה שֶּׁבְּתוֹכוֹ לַקֹּדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the question of בני רבי חייא to רב כהנא that began just before this section.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does כלי מצרף require the contents to physically touch, or does it work even when they are apart?

steps.title: The vessel joins its contents even without contact
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא answers from the exact wording of the משנה: it says 'מצרף' (joins), not 'מחבר' (connects), so it works in every case.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Did we learn 'a vessel connects'? We learned 'a vessel joins', meaning in any case at all.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא answers that both parts become disqualified, because the vessel joins them even if they do not touch.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He proves it from the wording of the משנה. 'מחבר' would suggest physical connection, but 'מצרף' means the vessel itself gathers its contents into one unit. So contact is not needed.

keyTerms.meaning: A vessel connects; this wording would suggest physical contact is needed
In any way at all, in every case
Did we learn? It points to the exact wording of a source

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic rule for the rest of the section: the vessel joins its contents even when they are physically separate.

phrases.english: He said to them:
phrases.notes: 'He' is רב כהנא, answering בני רבי חייא.

phrases.english: Did we learn 'a vessel connects'?
We learned 'a vessel joins', in any case at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי תְּנַן ״כְּלִי מְחַבֵּר״? ״כְּלִי מְצָרֵף״ תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The vessel joins even separated contents, because the משנה says מצרף, not מחבר.

steps.title: Another portion placed between the two parts
steps.stepSummary: Next question: if someone puts another portion between the two parts and the טבול יום touches it, are the first two parts also disqualified?
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone inserted another one between them, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: בני רבי חייא ask a follow-up question: what if an extra portion is placed in the bowl between the two parts?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since step 2 taught that the vessel joins everything inside it, maybe this new portion is also joined to the others. If so, touching it would disqualify the original two parts.

keyTerms.meaning: He stretched out or inserted
Between them

phrases.english: If someone inserted another one between them,
phrases.notes: Another half-עשרון was put in the bowl between the two parts, and the טבול יום touched that one.

phrases.english: what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: הוֹשִׁיט אֶחָד לְבֵינֵיהֶן מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the answer of step 2 and tests how far it reaches.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the vessel also join an outside portion placed in it, so that touching it disqualifies the original parts?

steps.title: A vessel only joins what needs the vessel
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא limits the rule: the vessel joins only something that needs the vessel to be sanctified. The extra portion does not need it, so it is not joined.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Something that needs the vessel, the vessel joins it. Something that does not need the vessel, the vessel does not join it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא answers that the extra portion is not joined, so touching it does not disqualify the original two parts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two halves of the original עשרון need the כלי to become sanctified, so the vessel joins them. The inserted portion does not need this vessel, so it stays outside the צירוף. This adds a limit to the rule of step 2.

keyTerms.meaning: Needs the vessel, in order to become sanctified
Joins it together with the other contents

steps.whatToRemember: כלי מצרף works even without physical contact, but only for items that need the כלי.

phrases.english: He said to them:
What needs the vessel, the vessel joins it;

phrases.aramaic: אֵין צָרִיךְ לִכְלִי – אֵין כְּלִי מְצָרְפוֹ.
phrases.english: what does not need the vessel, the vessel does not join it.

steps.triggerLanguage: צָרִיךְ לִכְלִי – כְּלִי מְצָרְפוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 3 by limiting the rule of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Only items that need the vessel are joined by it; the inserted portion is not.

steps.title: The טבול יום puts his finger between the parts
steps.stepSummary: Third question: if the טבול יום puts his finger into the space between the two parts without touching either, are they disqualified?
steps.simpleTranslation: If a טבול יום inserted his finger between them, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: בני רבי חייא ask whether just putting a finger into the bowl's space, without touching the flour, disqualifies it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the vessel unites its contents, maybe entering the space inside the vessel counts like touching what is in it. The question tests whether the vessel's airspace matters.

keyTerms.meaning: His finger

phrases.aramaic: הוֹשִׁיט טְבוּל יוֹם אֶת אֶצְבָּעוֹ בֵּינֵיהֶן,
phrases.english: If a טבול יום inserted his finger between them,
what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: הוֹשִׁיט טְבוּל יוֹם אֶת אֶצְבָּעוֹ בֵּינֵיהֶן מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new follow-up question in the same series.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does entering the airspace of the vessel, without contact, disqualify the contents?

steps.title: Only a כלי חרס works through its airspace
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא answers that only a כלי חרס works through its airspace. This bowl is not one, so the finger in the space does nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: You have nothing that conveys impurity through its airspace except an earthenware vessel alone.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא answers that the flour stays pure, because airspace only matters for a כלי חרס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: טומאה through אויר, the inside space of a vessel, is a special law found only with כלי חרס. Without that special law, a finger in the empty space counts as no contact at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Works with טומאה through its inside airspace, without contact
Earthenware vessel, which has the special law of airspace
Alone, only

steps.whatToRemember: A vessel can join its contents without contact, but only a כלי חרס makes its airspace count; a finger in the space of any other vessel does nothing.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two ideas: the vessel joining its contents (צירוף) is not the same as airspace טומאה. The first works with any vessel; the second only with a כלי חרס.

phrases.english: He said to them:
You have nothing that conveys impurity through its airspace
except an earthenware vessel alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין לְךָ דָּבָר שֶׁמְּטַמֵּא מֵאֲוִירוֹ אֶלָּא כְּלִי חֶרֶס בִּלְבַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Airspace only matters for a כלי חרס, so the finger in the space does not disqualify the flour.

steps.title: רב כהנא asks: can you take the קומץ from one part for the other?
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא asks whether the vessel's joining of two separated parts of a מנחה is strong enough, from the Torah, to let the קמיצה from one part count for the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then רב כהנא himself asked them: What is the law about taking the handful from this part on behalf of that part? Is the joining by the vessel from the Torah or from the Rabbis?
steps.whatsHappening: Until now the sons of רבי חייא asked and רב כהנא answered. Now רב כהנא asks them a question about the same two-part מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps showed that the vessel joins the two parts for טומאה. Now the question is whether this joining also counts for the עבודה of קמיצה. If the joining is only rabbinic (a strict rule for טומאה), it cannot make a קמיצה from one part valid for the whole מנחה.

keyTerms.meaning: To take the handful (קומץ) from a מנחה
Joining: the vessel treats separate parts as one unit
From the Torah
From the Rabbis

steps.whyThisMatters: If the joining is from the Torah, it has real power to unite the מנחה for קמיצה. If it is only rabbinic, it works only to be strict with טומאה, not to make a קמיצה valid.

phrases.english: He himself then asked them:
phrases.notes: "He" is רב כהנא, and "them" are the sons of רבי חייא who were asking him until now.

phrases.english: What is the law about taking the handful from this on behalf of that?
phrases.notes: This means the two halves of one מנחה sitting in one bowl without touching.

phrases.english: Is the joining from the Torah or from the Rabbis?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַר אִיהוּ בְּעָא מִינַּיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After answering three questions about טומאה, רב כהנא asks a new question about קמיצה in the same case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the vessel's צירוף is from the Torah (so קמיצה from one part works for the whole) or only rabbinic.

steps.title: They know a similar case: two מנחות that got mixed
steps.stepSummary: The sons of רבי חייא say they never heard this exact case, but they quote a משנה about two mixed מנחות that may be similar.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: This case we did not hear, but we heard something like it. As the משנה teaches: Two מנחות whose handful was not yet taken, which got mixed together: if he can take a handful from this one by itself and from that one by itself, they are valid. If not, they are invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: They answer by quoting a related משנה. This sets up the proof that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that two mixed מנחות are still valid if a separate קומץ can be taken from each. The idea is that some of each מנחה is stuck in the mix, so you take the קומץ from the part that is not mixed. That is like taking from one part for another.

keyTerms.meaning: Something like it, a similar case
Flour offerings
Got mixed together
Valid / invalid

phrases.english: They said to him: This we did not hear,
but something like it we did hear,
as we learned: Two meal offerings from which the handful was not taken
and they became mixed with each other,

phrases.aramaic: אִם יָכוֹל לִקְמוֹץ מִזּוֹ בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָהּ
phrases.english: if he can take a handful from this one by itself
and from that one by itself, they are valid,
and if not, they are invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: זוֹ לֹא שָׁמַעְנוּ, כַּיּוֹצֵא בּוֹ שָׁמַעְנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב כהנא's question by bringing a similar משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No direct tradition, but a משנה about two mixed מנחות may show that the vessel joins the parts.

steps.title: The proof: the mixed part does not touch, yet the קמיצה works
steps.stepSummary: בני רבי חייא draw the proof: the part of the מנחה that is mixed in does not touch the part used for the קומץ, yet the מנחה is valid, so the vessel must join them.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, when he can take a handful, they are valid. Why? This part that is mixed in does not touch the rest!
steps.whatsHappening: בני רבי חייא explain how the משנה answers רב כהנא's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some of each מנחה is inside the mixed area and seems separate from the part where the קומץ is taken. Still, the משנה says it is valid. That suggests the vessel's joining is strong enough to let one part count for another, just as רב כהנא asked.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case, at least
Why?
Touched

phrases.english: In any case, when he can take a handful, they are valid,
why?
That part which is mixed in does not touch!
phrases.notes: He means the mixed part does not touch the part the קומץ is taken from, so only the vessel could be joining them.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי יָכוֹל לִקְמוֹץ מִיהָא כְּשֵׁירוֹת, אַמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the משנה quoted in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: That the vessel joins separated parts of a מנחה, so קמיצה from one part works for the other.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of two mixed מנחות that are valid if a separate קומץ can be taken from each.

steps.title: רבא: maybe the clumps are still connected, like a comb
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects the proof: maybe the משנה is about clumps divided like the teeth of a comb, which are still connected at the base.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Perhaps it is talking about clumps that are divided, made like a comb.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on the proof from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A comb has separate teeth, but they are all attached to one back. So the mixed clump and the clump used for the קומץ may really still be connected. If so, the משנה says nothing about parts that truly do not touch, and רב כהנא's question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps
Clumps (of flour mixed with oil)
Divided, split up
A comb

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the vessel does not join. He only says this משנה does not prove it, because the parts may still be touching.
steps.whatToRemember: The proof from the mixed מנחות fails, since the clumps may be connected like comb teeth. The question of whether the joining is from the Torah is not yet answered.

phrases.english: Rava said: Perhaps it is about clumps
that are divided, made like a comb.
phrases.notes: Like comb teeth: separate at the tips but joined at the base, so the whole מנחה is still touching.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: דִּלְמָא בְּגוּשִּׁין הַמְחוּלָּקִין הָעֲשׂוּיִין כְּמַסְרֵק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof drawn in step 9 by reading the משנה as a case where the parts are connected.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the משנה only. It does not settle רב כהנא's question either way.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the parts were fully separate, but the משנה could be about clumps still connected like the teeth of a comb.

steps.title: So what is the final ruling?
steps.stepSummary: Since רבא pushed off the proof from the משנה, the גמרא asks what the ruling is on רב כהנא's question.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the conclusion on this matter?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the final answer is to the question of whether a vessel joins two separated parts of a מנחה. This short line sets up רבא's proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof from the mixed מנחות fell apart, so the question from step 7 is open again. The גמרא now looks for a different source.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the conclusion about it? This asks for the final ruling on an open question.

phrases.english: What is the conclusion about it?
phrases.notes: 'It' means רב כהנא's question from step 7: does the vessel join the two parts of the מנחה?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי הָוֵי עֲלַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof in step 9 was pushed off in step 10, the גמרא reopens the original question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a vessel joins two non-touching halves of an עשרון so that one קמיצה counts for both.

steps.title: רבא's proof from 'and he shall take up from it'
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes a ברייתא: you cannot take a קומץ from an עשרון split between two vessels. He infers that one vessel that looks like two vessels does allow it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Come and hear, as a ברייתא teaches: 'And he shall take up from it' means from what is connected. You may not bring an עשרון in two vessels and take the קומץ. This implies that with one vessel that is like two vessels, you may take the קומץ.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a ברייתא that forbids taking a קומץ when the מנחה is split between two vessels. From this he infers that if it is all in one vessel, even when it looks like two separate piles, the קמיצה works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא learns from the פסוק that the קומץ must come from a connected מנחה. Since it only rules out two separate vessels, רבא reads it to mean that one vessel holding separated parts counts as connected. If so, the vessel joins the parts, which answers רב כהנא's question.

keyTerms.meaning: From what is connected. The קומץ must be taken from a מנחה that is joined together.
A tenth of an איפה, the standard measure of a מנחה.
He takes the קומץ, the handful removed from the מנחה.
Similar to, resembling.

phrases.english: Rava said: Come and hear, as it is taught:
"And he shall take up from it": from what is connected,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא יָבִיא עִשָּׂרוֹן בִּשְׁנֵי כֵּלִים וְיִקְמוֹץ.
phrases.english: that one should not bring a tenth in two vessels and take the handful.

phrases.aramaic: הָא בִּכְלִי אֶחָד דּוּמְיָא דִּשְׁנֵי כֵּלִים – קָמֵיץ.
phrases.english: This implies that in one vessel that is like two vessels, he may take the handful.
phrases.notes: 'Like two vessels' means everything sits in one vessel, but the parts are apart and not touching, just like our case.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request in step 11 with a new proof from a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That a vessel joins two separated parts of a מנחה for קמיצה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on 'וְהֵרִים מִמֶּנּוּ', read through what it implies (הָא): only two vessels are forbidden, so one vessel that looks like two is allowed.

steps.title: אביי: 'two vessels' may mean a קפיזא carved inside a קב
steps.stepSummary: אביי suggests that the ברייתא's 'two vessels' means two hollows in one container that are joined at the top but separated at the bottom.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Maybe 'two vessels' means something like a קפיזא hollowed out inside a קב. Even though the contents mix on top, since the wall of the קפיזא separates them below, they count as two vessels.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רבא's proof by giving a narrower meaning of 'two vessels.' It could be one container with an inner wall that splits the bottom into two hollows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even this case counts as 'two vessels,' then the ברייתא's ban covers parts that touch at the top but are split at the bottom. That changes what the inference 'one vessel like two vessels' can mean, which אביי explains in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps. It introduces another way to read a source, which weakens a proof.
What is the case? How do we picture it?
A small measuring vessel.
A קב, a larger measure.
The partition, the dividing wall.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Perhaps, what is the case of two vessels?
For example, a kefiza within a kav,
phrases.notes: Picture one big container with a smaller hollow carved into its bottom. Its wall does not reach the top.

phrases.english: where even though they are mixed together above,
since the partition of the kefiza separates them below.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: דִּילְמָא שְׁנֵי כֵּלִים הֵיכִי דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's proof by giving a narrow meaning to 'two vessels' in the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Partial. It redefines the cases in the ברייתא, so the inference no longer reaches our case.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבא assumed 'two vessels' means truly separate vessels. It could mean one container split at the bottom, with the contents touching on top.

steps.title: אביי: 'one vessel like two' may be a hen trough, so our case stays open
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the allowed case may be a hen trough, where the contents touch below. Our case, where the parts never touch, is still unresolved.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the case of one vessel like two vessels? Something like a hen trough. Even though a partition divides it, the contents still touch. But here, where the parts do not touch at all, you should still ask the question.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes his pushback. The allowed case in the ברייתא may be one where the parts still touch underneath, so it says nothing about parts that never touch, and the question stays open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a hen trough the dividers are on top and the contents connect below, so the parts are really joined by touching, not by the vessel. Our מנחה halves do not touch at all, which means the ברייתא does not prove the vessel joins them. רב כהנא's question remains unresolved.

keyTerms.meaning: A hen trough. Its dividers sit on top while the food or water underneath is connected.
Touching.
You should ask it. The question still stands.

steps.whatToRemember: Both proofs (from the משנה in step 9 and from the ברייתא here) were pushed off for the same reason. Each could be about parts that still touch somewhere. Whether a vessel alone joins parts that do not touch at all is left unresolved.
steps.confusionAlert: The two cases are mirror images. In the קפיזא inside a קב, the parts touch on TOP but are split at the BOTTOM, and that counts as two vessels (forbidden). In the hen trough, the parts are split on TOP but touch at the BOTTOM, and that counts as one vessel (allowed).

phrases.aramaic: הָא כְּלִי אֶחָד דּוּמְיָא דִּשְׁנֵי כֵּלִים, הֵיכִי דָּמֵי?
phrases.english: And one vessel that is like two vessels, what is the case?
For example, a hen trough,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּמִיפַּסְקָן מְחִיצָתָא הָא נְגִיעַ,
phrases.english: and even though a partition divides them, they are touching,
phrases.notes: The partition divides the top, but underneath the contents still connect.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא דְּלָא נְגִיעַ כְּלָל – תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ.
phrases.english: but here, where they do not touch at all, you should raise the question.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא כְּלִי אֶחָד דּוּמְיָא דִּשְׁנֵי כֵּלִים, הֵיכִי דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes אביי's rejection by redefining the second case in the ברייתא, and ends with the question unresolved.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Full. The ברייתא no longer proves anything about parts that never touch.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The allowed 'one vessel' case may involve contents that touch below. Their touching joins them, not the vessel.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The question of whether a vessel joins parts that do not touch at all (תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ) remains unresolved.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: a vessel's joining combined with a water connection
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks a new question: what happens when a vessel's joining and a water connection work together?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה asked: What is the law when there is joining by a vessel together with connection by water?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה opens a new question. Two halves sit in one vessel without touching, and one of them is linked by water to another half outside the vessel. If a טבול יום touches the other half inside the vessel, does the half outside become פסול too?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each kind of link might work on its own. Here the question is whether they can be chained, so that a פסול passes through the vessel's joining and then through the water to a part outside. This builds on the vessel-joining idea and tests how far it reaches.

keyTerms.meaning: Joining by a vessel. The vessel makes the separate parts inside it count as one.
Connection by water. Liquid links two things together.
What is the law? This opens an unresolved question.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya raises a dilemma:
Joining by a vessel and connection by water, what is the law?
phrases.notes: The question is very short. Picture two halves joined by a vessel, one of them linked by water to a half outside, and a טבול יום touching the first half.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first question is left open, a new question builds on the idea of a vessel joining its contents.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a vessel's joining and a water connection can combine to pass a פסול from a טבול יום's touch to a portion outside the vessel.

steps.title: Does the vessel's joining reach an item outside it?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה spells out his question. The משנה says a vessel joins what is inside it. Does that only cover what is inside, or also an outside item linked to the inside by water?
steps.simpleTranslation: When the משנה taught that a vessel joins what is inside it for קודש, maybe that only applies to what is inside, not to what is outside. Or maybe, since the outside part is connected, it counts as connected.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the two sides of רבי ירמיה's question from step 15. Inside the vessel, everything is joined. Is an item outside the vessel, linked by water to the inside, also joined?
steps.deeperAnalysis: One side says the rule of כלי מצרף only covers what is physically inside the vessel. The other side says the outside item is connected through the water to something inside, so it is part of the group. The question is whether the two kinds of connection can work together like a chain.

keyTerms.meaning: A vessel joins its contents, so impurity on one part spreads to everything in it
For sacred food (קדשים), which has stricter impurity rules
What is inside / what is outside
Since it is connected, it counts as connected

phrases.english: When we learned: "a vessel joins"
what is inside it, with regard to sacred food
this applies to what is inside
but to what is outside, no
or perhaps
since it is connected, it is connected
phrases.notes: He means the outside item is linked by water to food inside the vessel.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי תְּנַן כְּלִי מְצָרֵף מַה שֶּׁבְּתוֹכוֹ לַקֹּדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the two sides of רבי ירמיה's question from step 15
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does צירוף כלי reach an item outside the vessel that is linked by water to the inside contents?

steps.title: Follow-up: what if the טבול יום touches the outside item?
steps.stepSummary: Suppose the outside item does count as connected. Now what if the טבול יום touches the outside item instead of the inside?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that since it is connected it counts as connected, then what about a water connection plus a vessel joining, where a טבול יום touched the outside item?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה asks a second question that builds on one answer to the first. He flips the case so the impurity starts outside the vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first question, impurity started inside and the doubt was whether it spreads out through the water. Now impurity starts outside, travels in through the water, and the doubt is whether the vessel then spreads it to all its contents. The 'if you say' format shows this second question only arises if the first is answered 'yes, connected'.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say: introduces a follow-up question built on one answer to the first
Someone who immersed today and is waiting for nightfall; he can still make קודש impure
A connection through water between two items
The joining a vessel creates among its contents

phrases.english: And if you say:
since it is connected, it is connected,
a water connection plus a vessel's joining,
and a טבול יום touched from the outside, what is the law?
phrases.notes: He touched the item outside the vessel, not the food inside.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם תִּימְצֵי לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a second question on one possible answer to step 16
steps.sheelahInformationSought: When impurity starts at the outside item, does the vessel's joining spread it to all the contents inside?

steps.title: Explaining the two sides of the follow-up question
steps.stepSummary: Maybe כלי מצרף only works when the inside is touched. Or maybe it makes no difference where the touch happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: When we learned 'a vessel joins', maybe that is only where he touched the inside, but not the outside. Or perhaps there is no difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the two possible views behind the follow-up question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One view: the vessel only joins its contents when the impurity reaches them directly from inside. If impurity enters through the outside item, only the one piece it reaches through the water becomes impure. The other view: once impurity reaches anything in the vessel, the vessel spreads it to everything, wherever it started.

keyTerms.meaning: This rule applies only to... (limits a rule)
Where he touched from the inside
There is no difference

phrases.english: When we learned "a vessel joins,"
this applies where he touched from the inside,
but from the outside, no,
or perhaps there is no difference?

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי תְּנַן כְּלִי מְצָרֵף הָנֵי מִילֵּי דְּנָגַע מִגַּוַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the two sides of the question asked in step 17
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does כלי מצרף depend on the impurity entering from inside the vessel?

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends רבי ירמיה's questions with תיקו: no answer is found.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says it cannot answer רבי ירמיה's question, so it is left open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source decides whether the vessel's joining and the water connection work together. The case stays a doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand: the question remains unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: רבי ירמיה's questions about combining a water connection with a vessel's joining, whether the touch is inside or outside, are left unresolved (תיקו).

phrases.english: Let it stand unresolved.

steps.triggerLanguage: תֵּיקוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question of steps 16 to 18 with no answer
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether צירוף כלי and חיבור מים combine is left unresolved.

steps.title: Can an already impure half pass on impurity again?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks about an עשרון split in two. One half became impure and was then put in a container with the other half. A טבול יום then touched the impure half. Does this new touch make the other half impure, or is the first half already 'full' of impurity?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: an עשרון was divided, one half became impure, and he put it in a container. Then a טבול יום touched that impure half. What is the law? Do we say it is already full of impurity, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא opens a new question. Can a new touch of impurity on something already impure count again, so the vessel spreads it to the other half?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half became impure before it was in the vessel with the other half, so that impurity did not spread. The new touch by the טבול יום happens while both are joined in the container. If the impure half is already 'full', the new touch does nothing and the other half stays pure. If not, the vessel spreads the new impurity to the second half.

keyTerms.meaning: A tenth of an איפה, the measure of flour for a מנחה
That he divided into two parts
A container or receptacle
It is already full of impurity, so it cannot become impure again

phrases.english: רבא asked:
A tenth that he divided,
and one of them became impure,
and he placed it in a container,
phrases.notes: He put it in together with the other, still pure half.

phrases.english: and then a טבול יום
touched that impure one, what is the law?
Do we say it is already full of impurity,
or not?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רָבָא עִשָּׂרוֹן שֶׁחִלְּקוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about כלי מצרף after רבי ירמיה's question ended in תיקו
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Can something already impure receive impurity again (or is it שבע לו טומאה), so that the vessel spreads the new impurity to the other half?

steps.title: אביי questions whether something can be 'full' of impurity
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges the idea behind רבא's question, that an already-impure item is 'full' of טומאה and cannot take on more. He begins quoting a משנה about a טמא sheet as his source.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Do we really say that something is 'full' of impurity? Didn't we learn in a משנה: a sheet that is impure...
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רבא's idea that an impure item is 'full' of טומאה. He starts quoting a משנה to prove his point, and the rest of that משנה comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's question depended on the idea of שבע ליה טומאה: once an item is impure, a new touch adds nothing. אביי attacks that idea itself and claims a משנה shows an impure item can still be affected by a new source of טומאה. Here we only hear the opening words, an impure sheet; the full proof follows.

keyTerms.meaning: It is 'full' of impurity. The idea that an already-impure item cannot take on more impurity.
Do we really say...? Introduces doubt about an idea someone assumed.
A sheet, a piece of cloth
Impure, ritually unclean

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not answering רבא's question directly. He is attacking the idea of being 'full' of impurity that one side of the question rests on.
steps.whyThisMatters: If אביי is right that no item is ever 'full' of טומאה, then one side of רבא's question falls away.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
And do we say that it is saturated with impurity?
phrases.notes: Literally 'it is full of impurity,' meaning it is already so impure that a new touch adds nothing.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in a משנה: a sheet that is impure

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמְרִינַן שְׂבַע לֵיהּ טוּמְאָה? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the 'full of impurity' idea that רבא's question in Step 20 depends on.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea of שבע ליה טומאה, that an already-impure item cannot become impure again.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה about an impure sheet seems to show that an item already טמא can still be affected by a new source of impurity. So no item is ever 'full' of טומאה.
